intelligenceEvents.title: Bank of Canada Decreases Overnight Rate by 50 bps to 3.25%
intelligenceEvents.summary: The Bank of Canada lowered its target for the overnight rate to 3.25%, citing cooling inflation and labor market stabilization.
intelligenceEvents.detailedAnalysis: Borrowers with adjustable-rate mortgages (ARM) or Home Equity Lines of Credit (HELOC) will see monthly interest charges decrease by approximately $31 per $100,000 borrowed balance.

source.name: Bank of Canada
source.organization: Banque du Canada
source.notes: Policy interest rate and overnight rate target.

intelligenceEvents.title: Federal Reserve Cuts Benchmark Fed Funds Rate to 4.50%
intelligenceEvents.summary: The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) decided to lower the target range for the federal funds rate by 25 basis points to 4.25%–4.50%.
intelligenceEvents.detailedAnalysis: Prime rate adjustments will flow into credit card APRs and variable business loans within 1-2 billing cycles. High Yield Savings Accounts (HYSA) yields are expected to ease from 4.8% to ~4.4%.

source.organization: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve

intelligenceEvents.title: India Union Budget 2025 Revises Section 115BAC Slabs and Hikes Standard Deduction
intelligenceEvents.summary: Ministry of Finance enhanced the standard deduction to ₹75,000 for salaried taxpayers under the New Tax Regime, widening 5% and 10% tax brackets.
intelligenceEvents.detailedAnalysis: Salaried employees earning ₹15,00,000 will save approximately ₹17,500 annually in net tax liability under the revised Section 115BAC structure.

source.name: Income Tax Department of India
source.organization: Ministry of Finance, Government of India
source.notes: Union Budget Finance Act Section 115BAC (New Tax Regime).

intelligenceEvents.title: Bank of England Reduces Base Rate to 4.75%
intelligenceEvents.summary: The Bank of England Monetary Policy Committee voted to cut the Bank Rate by 25 basis points to 4.75%.
intelligenceEvents.detailedAnalysis: Fixed-rate mortgage renewal quotes for 2-year and 5-year terms have improved by 15-20 bps across High Street lenders (Barclays, Nationwide, HSBC).

source.organization: Monetary Policy Committee (MPC)
source.notes: Official Bank Rate decision.
